record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider the variations of Hopf vector fields on S^{2m+1} that start at a Hopf vector field, decrease volume for small positive parameter values, and converge to a parallel-transport vector field. For which m and r are these variations volume-decreasing for the entire parameter interval, not only infinitesimally near the Hopf vector field?

evidence.quote: These variations starting at Hopf vector fields are decreasing volume for small t
we don’t know if they are volume decreasing for all t.

artifact.category_tag: Volume of unit vector fields on spheres
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on the volume functional for unit vector fields on odd-dimensional spheres establishes that Hopf vector fields minimize volume on S^3 (Gluck–Ziller) but fail to be minima on S^{2m+1} for m≥2 (Pedersen), and explicit variations from Hopf to parallel-transport vector fields are known to be infinitesimally volume-decreasing. However, no source verifies that these variations are volume-decreasing throughout the whole parameter interval for general (m,r); the question is explicitly posed as open in the survey from which it originates, and no subsequent resolution is found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: A critical radius for unit Hopf vector fields on spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of the Hopf field depends on radius; instability occurs precisely if and only if the Hopf field cannot be minimum.
status_evidence.claim: Hopf vector fields are not always volume-minimizing on higher-dimensional spheres, motivating the study of variations toward other critical vector fields.

status_evidence.title: On the volume of a unit vector field on the three-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf vector fields minimize the volume on S^3; Pedersen exhibited vector fields with less volume than Hopf for dimensions ≥ 5.
status_evidence.claim: For m≥2, Hopf fields are not minima, so global behavior of natural variations to parallel-transport fields is nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems regarding the volume functional, including monotonicity of Hopf-to-parallel-transport variations.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of global monotonicity of these variations is stated as open.
